summary: Fixed the two failures (test_nested_overrides_limit_raising on asyncio and trio) but have not re-run the tests. The outermost middleware used to reject a declared Content-Length over its own limit before routing, so an inner limit could never raise the outer one. It now checks the declared length lazily on each receive call, against the current shared limit, before reading from the server. A nested instance still rejects up front against its own limit. An oversized declared length is therefore rejected when the app first reads the body, not before the app is called. I updated the test for the declared-length check to match, and changed the `run` helper in the test file to consume the chunk list in place.
